result:
This confirms and enriches everything I traced in the code. I now have the full path. Here's the explanation.

## The path from "due date passes" to "one alert, one person"

**What starts the check.** `src/instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` runs once per server process and calls `startScheduler()` from `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`. That starts a `setInterval` ticking every 60 seconds (`TICK_INTERVAL_MS`). Each `tick(now)` checks `CADENCE_MINUTES` and finds `"overdue-issues"` due once every 60 minutes; when due, it `enqueue()`s a job into the in-process queue (`src/server/jobs/queue.ts`) and immediately `drain()`s it, which dynamically imports and calls `runOverdueIssueJob(now)` from `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`. (There's also an HTTP-triggerable path, `POST /api/cron/overdue` in `src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`, guarded by `assertCronSecret`, for an external cron caller to invoke the same function directly — either way the entry point is `runOverdueIssueJob`.)

**How the set of issues is narrowed.** Inside `runOverdueIssueJob`, `shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_ONLY)` (from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`) is asserted true as a defensive guard — archived issues must never count as overdue. It then walks orgs in pages via `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(ORG_BATCH)` (50 orgs per pass) and, per org, calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`). That query is the real filter: live (non-archived) issues, `dueAt` non-null and less than `now`, and status still in `["backlog","todo","in_progress","in_review"]` — i.e. not `done`, not archived.

**What the checking component does and doesn't own.** For each returned issue, the job checks its own in-process `reported: Set<string>` — if the issue's id is already in it, it's skipped. Otherwise it calls `emit("issue.overdue", { orgId, actorId: null, occurredAt, issueId, projectId, dueAt, assigneeId })` via `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, then adds the id to `reported`. The job explicitly does no notification work itself ("announce, don't act" per its doc comment) — it never writes a `Notification` row, decides a channel, or contacts anyone. That's entirely delegated to whoever subscribes to `issue.overdue` on the bus.

**What stops repeat announcements.** The `reported` `Set` is the dedup mechanism: as long as the process stays up, a still-open overdue issue is only emitted once, no matter how many hourly ticks pass. It is deliberately in-memory only (not a DB column) — a process restart clears it, so the first sweep after a deploy or crash will re-announce every currently-overdue issue once more. `resetOverdueTracking()` exists only to reset this set between tests.

**How the alert reaches one specific person.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` is wired up at process start (imported transitively by `event-registry.ts`'s `registerEventHandlers()`, also called from `instrumentation.ts`). Its `registerFanOut()` subscribes to `issue.overdue`; the handler bails out if `assigneeId` is null, otherwise calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], {...})`. `notify()` looks up that one recipient's stored preference via `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "issue_overdue")` and turns it into a channel list with `resolveChannels()` — `null` preference falls back to `DEFAULT_CHANNELS = ["in_app", "email"]`; an explicit preference yields `in_app` if enabled, and `email` only if `preference.email` is true and (not `digestOnly`, or `digestOnly` with the org's `digest_email` flag enabled — meaning digest subscribers get folded into the daily digest email built by `digest-service.ts`/`digest-email-job.ts` instead of an immediate one). If the resolved channel list is empty (everything muted) the recipient is skipped entirely. Otherwise `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` writes one row scoped to that `recipientId`, carrying the allowed `channels` — that row is what the in-app bell/notification list later queries by `recipientId`, so only that one assignee ever sees it.
